Key takeaways Business-to-business (B2B) marketing is a type of marketing that businesses use when focusing on promoting goods and services to other businesses rather than to consumers, and it involves strategies such as B2B content marketing, social media marketing, and email marketing. B2B content marketing helps you rank in search engine results, which can increase your visibility with potential customers, and help build trust using various types of content, including explainer videos, educational content regarding industry trends, and customer testimonials. You can build your B2B digital marketing strategy by identifying your brand positioning and how set your brand apart from its competition, describing your target buyers, building your brand voice, and selecting B2B marketing channels. B2B marketing means targeting decision-makers at organizations, typically based on logical motics such as return on investment. Read on to learn more about B2B marketing, including common strategies and how to develop a marketing plan for your business. Afterward, if you want to build foundational marketing skills, consider enrolling in the Google Digital Marketing & E-commerce Professional Certificate . It takes an average of six months to complete at a flexible pace and offers opportunities to learn digital marketing fundamentals, become familiar with spreadsheets, and develop skills in social media marketing, relationship management, and media planning. What is B2B marketing? Business-to-business, or B2B, marketing is the process of promoting products and services to other companies to help them improve their operations. It helps create demand and brand awareness. B2B companies often offer products and services such as software-as-a-service (SaaS), professional services, consulting, manufacturing, and wholesale products.Some B2B companies are large and also offer products directly to consumers. For example, Amazon, Meta, and Apple all blur the lines between the two and require both B2B and business-to-consumer (B2C) marketing. Other real-world examples of B2B companies include: Microsoft Salesforce Mailchimp When selling to other companies, remember that B2B marketing involves considerations and best practices that differ from those associated with marketing to individual consumers (B2C). For example, B2B customers generally look for products and services that will contribute to a healthier bottom line while avoiding investments with a low likelihood of a return. Considering that businesses may be responsible for payroll and other large business expenses, there may be more at stake for B2B than B2C customers, so when marketing, you’d want to bear this difference in mind. Explore other differences in the chart below: B2B B2C What it is Marketing to the decision makers at organizations Marketing to individual consumers Product examples Software, office equipment, and supplies, co-working spaces Food, clothing, electronic devices, books, media subscriptions Service examples Consulting and training, web or graphic design, product distribution, ad campaign management Tutoring, hair styling, health care, home cleaning, car repair Buying motives Logic: What’s the financial ROI of an investment? What’s the expertise level of a service provider? Emotions: Will this product solve a problem or fulfill a desire? Sales cycle Longer sales cycle as decision makers consider the return on investment Shorter sales cycle, especially for impulse purchases Market research focus Firmographics of businesses and psychographics of decision makers Demographics and psychographics of individual consumers 7 common B2B digital marketing strategies B2B marketing strategies, which include B2B-focused content marketing, social media marketing, email marketing, and event marketing, can help connect buyers with products and services using a combination of data and content to achieve results. Discover some common B2B marketing channels , both digital and offline, as well as best practices for promoting your business on these channels to help plan your next steps. B2B content marketing Content marketing , particularly SEO content on your website , is an effective way to reach a target audience of B2B customers. Focused content can build trust with decision-makers, increase your website’s ranking in search engine results, and provide a basis for marketing efforts on other channels. Different types of content that work well for a B2B audience include the following: Thought leadership and educational content on important industry trends and strategies that your target B2B customers can use Videos explaining how your products and services can help B2B customers Webpages explaining your company’s method of prioritizing diversity, equity, and inclusion, and what these efforts mean for your target B2B customer Customer testimonials Read more: How to Develop a Content Strategy: A Step-by-Step Guide B2B social media marketing To attract B2B customers on different social media platforms, adopt practices that are specific to a business-oriented audience, and leverage the power of videos for product demonstrations, tutorials, industry highlights, behind-the-scenes content, case studies, “about us” stories, and business-building strategies. Additional strategies to consider include the following: Tailor your posts to each platform. For example, you could repurpose long-form content into a Tweetable tip, an infographic for Instagram, and an excerpt for LinkedIn. Set up in-platform purchase and subscription options on social media. Algorithms may promote this content to more viewers, as it doesn’t lead users away from the platform. Partner with micro-influencers in your niche (users with 10,000 to 99,999 followers) to gain access to their loyal, targeted followers. B2B podcasting Podcasting can be a great way to reach B2B customers and provide them with informative content in audio format. By discussing topics that help businesses thrive, your podcast can establish you as a B2B thought leader. Topics might include: Leadership strategies Industry news and trends B2B customer success stories E-commerce best practices B2B email marketing Email marketing can be an effective way to build relationships with B2B customers and convert leads (potential customers or prospects) into buyers. Artificial intelligence (AI) tools can help optimize email campaigns, drive increased personalization, and automate content generation directed to specific buyers. Additional email marketing strategies to consider include the following: To build your subscriber base, design a lead-capture landing page that addresses a top-of-mind problem or need for your target B2B customers and promises a solution in the form of a lead magnet, such as a downloadable report or a free video tutorial. Make sure your lead magnet actually provides the solution promised on the landing page and demonstrates how your company can help other businesses operate more smoothly. Divide your subscribers into smaller segments based on their roles within a decision-making unit, the kind of business, where they are in the customer journey, and other factors, so that you can tailor email marketing content accordingly. Include attention-grabbing words in your email subject lines, such as solutions to a problem or product offers, to encourage B2B email subscribers to click. Craft each email message to deliver value and lead subscribers to a purchase decision. Emails can expound upon social media and content marketing pieces, offer exclusive information, invite subscribers to complete a survey, shape future content, and announce new products. B2B event marketing Hosting, attending, and sponsoring events, either in person or online, can increase your brand’s exposure and generate qualified leads. Successful B2B events can take on many forms, including: Workshops, classes, and webinars on topics of interest to your target B2B customers Networking events, exhibitions, and trade shows, where you can build relationships with company decision-makers in your target market and introduce them to your products and services Professional conferences where your target B2B customers can learn new information and network with peers Parties, performances, dinners, and other social events to entertain target B2B customers and offer individualized or VIP experiences B2B marketing word-of-mouth and referrals Loyal and satisfied customers can be a great source of new leads, especially in B2B marketing. When a business recommends your product or service and can quantify a positive outcome, it carries authority. To encourage customers to make thoughtful referrals, you might offer referral bonuses or set up an affiliate program . Paid search Paid search, also known as pay-per-click (PPC) advertising, refers to a strategy that marketers use to leverage search engine results pages (SERPs). Ads typically appear at the top or bottom of a search engine results page (SERP), and when an internet user clicks on an ad, the advertiser pays a fee. This strategy can support your B2B efforts by targeting ads to businesses looking for a specific solution that you can provide. To succeed, you'll need compelling ad copy, strategic keywords (search queries B2B customers use to search the internet), and data-driven insights. Build your B2B digital marketing agency strategy A B2B marketing strategy can have a measurable impact on your business as you expand into new markets for your products and services. Follow the steps below to begin building your B2B marketing strategy, starting with positioning your brand to stand out amongst your competitors. Determine your brand’s positioning. Brand positioning is the combination of factors that differentiate your brand from competitors in the minds of your ideal customers. Clear brand positioning can help you build brand equity and, thus, make your B2B marketing efforts more effective. How will your B2B products and services help businesses succeed better than competitors’ offerings ? What associations, ideas, feelings, and concepts will your brand create in customers’ minds? What will they believe about your products and services? What factors will inspire loyalty in your customers? How to create a B2B marketing agency brand positioning statement Use answers to the above questions to craft a brand positioning statement: [B2B audience] will choose [product/service] to experience [benefits and outcomes], because [B2B audience’s beliefs]. Describe your buyer personas. Create a distinct and detailed buyer persona for each type of business you serve. Start by gathering firmographic data (how different organizations behave) on the kinds of businesses you want to target, as well as psychographic data (how individuals behave) on decision-making units within these businesses, using the prompts below to start. Firmographic data on businesses: How would you describe the industry your target business is a part of, including key players, trends, opportunities, and untapped markets? What kinds of products or services do your target businesses offer? What types of consumers do they serve? How many employees work at these businesses? What’s the average annual revenue? How are these organizations structured in terms of leadership, departments, teams, and individual contributors? Psychographic data on decision-makers: What is the role of each decision-maker within your target businesses, and how will they interact with you during the sales process? What motivates these decision-makers professionally? What inspires them to work in this industry? Develop a brand voice. Your brand’s voice is essential to connecting with customers, personalizing their experience with your B2B products and services, and inspiring their trust in your business solutions. The brand voice will shape how you craft every email, social media caption, video script, piece of long-form content, web copy, and more. When conducting B2B market research, collect insights into the language that company decision-makers use to describe their challenges and goals. Draw from customer language to develop a distinct, empathetic brand voice. Select your B2B marketing channels. While it’s a good practice to build a presence and create customer experiences on multiple channels, don’t feel pressured to be on every channel . Prioritize the channels where your target B2B customers are most likely to engage with your content. Create a seamless omnichannel customer journey to increase loyalty and retention rates. Make sure you tell your full brand story on every channel so that your target B2B customers fully understand your offerings, value proposition, what you stand for, and how to take action. Identify your B2B marketing tactics. Once you’ve selected your marketing channels, your next step is to identify the specific tactics you’ll use to reach your target B2B customers. Four examples of tactics to implement include the following: Offer a freemium service or a trial period so B2B customers can experience the impact of your offerings on their operations. Take an account-based marketing approach by networking with contacts at key business targets, building rapport with them, personalizing the communications, and encouraging sales. Use cause-based marketing to design products and campaigns in collaboration with charitable organizations, demonstrating your business's commitment to creating a better world. Create a more impactful, detailed customer journey for a longer sales cycle. You can do this by delivering content that supports buying decisions and emphasizes the outcomes and benefits your products offer. What is B2B marketing? Business-to-business, or B2B, marketing is the process of promoting products and services to other companies to help them improve their operations. It helps create demand and brand awareness. B2B companies often offer products and services such as software-as-a-service (SaaS), professional services, consulting, manufacturing, and wholesale products.Some B2B companies are large and also offer products directly to consumers. For example, Amazon, Meta, and Apple all blur the lines between the two and require both B2B and business-to-consumer (B2C) marketing. Other real-world examples of B2B companies include: Microsoft Salesforce Mailchimp When selling to other companies, remember that B2B marketing involves considerations and best practices that differ from those associated with marketing to individual consumers (B2C). For example, B2B customers generally look for products and services that will contribute to a healthier bottom line while avoiding investments with a low likelihood of a return. Considering that businesses may be responsible for payroll and other large business expenses, there may be more at stake for B2B than B2C customers, so when marketing, you’d want to bear this difference in mind. What’s the expertise level of a service provider? Emotions: Will this product solve a problem or fulfill a desire? Sales cycle Longer sales cycle as decision makers consider the return on investment Shorter sales cycle, especially for impulse purchases Market research focus Firmographics of businesses and psychographics of decision makers Demographics and psychographics of individual consumers 7 common B2B digital marketing strategies B2B marketing strategies, which include B2B-focused content marketing, social media marketing, email marketing, and event marketing, can help connect buyers with products and services using a combination of data and content to achieve results. Discover some common B2B marketing channels , both digital and offline, as well as best practices for promoting your business on these channels to help plan your next steps. B2B content marketing Content marketing , particularly SEO content on your website , is an effective way to reach a target audience of B2B customers. Focused content can build trust with decision-makers, increase your website’s ranking in search engine results, and provide a basis for marketing efforts on other channels. Different types of content that work well for a B2B audience include the following: Thought leadership and educational content on important industry trends and strategies that your target B2B customers can use Videos explaining how your products and services can help B2B customers Webpages explaining your company’s method of prioritizing diversity, equity, and inclusion, and what these efforts mean for your target B2B customer Customer testimonials Read more: How to Develop a Content Strategy: A Step-by-Step Guide B2B social media marketing To attract B2B customers on different social media platforms, adopt practices that are specific to a business-oriented audience, and leverage the power of videos for product demonstrations, tutorials, industry highlights, behind-the-scenes content, case studies, “about us” stories, and business-building strategies. Additional strategies to consider include the following: Tailor your posts to each platform. For example, you could repurpose long-form content into a Tweetable tip, an infographic for Instagram, and an excerpt for LinkedIn. Set up in-platform purchase and subscription options on social media. Algorithms may promote this content to more viewers, as it doesn’t lead users away from the platform. Partner with micro-influencers in your niche (users with 10,000 to 99,999 followers) to gain access to their loyal, targeted followers. B2B podcasting Podcasting can be a great way to reach B2B customers and provide them with informative content in audio format. By discussing topics that help businesses thrive, your podcast can establish you as a B2B thought leader. Topics might include: Leadership strategies Industry news and trends B2B customer success stories E-commerce best practices B2B email marketing Email marketing can be an effective way to build relationships with B2B customers and convert leads (potential customers or prospects) into buyers. Artificial intelligence (AI) tools can help optimize email campaigns, drive increased personalization, and automate content generation directed to specific buyers. Additional email marketing strategies to consider include the following: To build your subscriber base, design a lead-capture landing page that addresses a top-of-mind problem or need for your target B2B customers and promises a solution in the form of a lead magnet, such as a downloadable report or a free video tutorial. Make sure your lead magnet actually provides the solution promised on the landing page and demonstrates how your company can help other businesses operate more smoothly. Divide your subscribers into smaller segments based on their roles within a decision-making unit, the kind of business, where they are in the customer journey, and other factors, so that you can tailor email marketing content accordingly. Include attention-grabbing words in your email subject lines, such as solutions to a problem or product offers, to encourage B2B email subscribers to click. Craft each email message to deliver value and lead subscribers to a purchase decision. Emails can expound upon social media and content marketing pieces, offer exclusive information, invite subscribers to complete a survey, shape future content, and announce new products. B2B event marketing Hosting, attending, and sponsoring events, either in person or online, can increase your brand’s exposure and generate qualified leads. Successful B2B events can take on many forms, including: Workshops, classes, and webinars on topics of interest to your target B2B customers Networking events, exhibitions, and trade shows, where you can build relationships with company decision-makers in your target market and introduce them to your products and services Professional conferences where your target B2B customers can learn new information and network with peers Parties, performances, dinners, and other social events to entertain target B2B customers and offer individualized or VIP experiences B2B marketing word-of-mouth and referrals Loyal and satisfied customers can be a great source of new leads, especially in B2B marketing. When a business recommends your product or service and can quantify a positive outcome, it carries authority. To encourage customers to make thoughtful referrals, you might offer referral bonuses or set up an affiliate program . Paid search Paid search, also known as pay-per-click (PPC) advertising, refers to a strategy that marketers use to leverage search engine results pages (SERPs). Ads typically appear at the top or bottom of a search engine results page (SERP), and when an internet user clicks on an ad, the advertiser pays a fee. This strategy can support your B2B efforts by targeting ads to businesses looking for a specific solution that you can provide. To succeed, you'll need compelling ad copy, strategic keywords (search queries B2B customers use to search the internet), and data-driven insights. Build your B2B digital marketing agency strategy A B2B marketing strategy can have a measurable impact on your business as you expand into new markets for your products and services. Follow the steps below to begin building your B2B marketing strategy, starting with positioning your brand to stand out amongst your competitors. Determine your brand’s positioning. Brand positioning is the combination of factors that differentiate your brand from competitors in the minds of your ideal customers. Clear brand positioning can help you build brand equity and, thus, make your B2B marketing efforts more effective. How will your B2B products and services help businesses succeed better than competitors’ offerings ? What associations, ideas, feelings, and concepts will your brand create in customers’ minds? What will they believe about your products and services? What factors will inspire loyalty in your customers? How to create a B2B marketing agency brand positioning statement Use answers to the above questions to craft a brand positioning statement: [B2B audience] will choose [product/service] to experience [benefits and outcomes], because [B2B audience’s beliefs]. Describe your buyer personas. Create a distinct and detailed buyer persona for each type of business you serve. Start by gathering firmographic data (how different organizations behave) on the kinds of businesses you want to target, as well as psychographic data (how individuals behave) on decision-making units within these businesses, using the prompts below to start. Firmographic data on businesses: How would you describe the industry your target business is a part of, including key players, trends, opportunities, and untapped markets? What kinds of products or services do your target businesses offer? What types of consumers do they serve? How many employees work at these businesses? What’s the average annual revenue? How are these organizations structured in terms of leadership, departments, teams, and individual contributors? Psychographic data on decision-makers: What is the role of each decision-maker within your target businesses, and how will they interact with you during the sales process? What motivates these decision-makers professionally? What inspires them to work in this industry? Develop a brand voice. Your brand’s voice is essential to connecting with customers, personalizing their experience with your B2B products and services, and inspiring their trust in your business solutions. The brand voice will shape how you craft every email, social media caption, video script, piece of long-form content, web copy, and more. When conducting B2B market research, collect insights into the language that company decision-makers use to describe their challenges and goals. Draw from customer language to develop a distinct, empathetic brand voice. Select your B2B marketing channels. While it’s a good practice to build a presence and create customer experiences on multiple channels, don’t feel pressured to be on every channel . Prioritize the channels where your target B2B customers are most likely to engage with your content. Create a seamless omnichannel customer journey to increase loyalty and retention rates. Make sure you tell your full brand story on every channel so that your target B2B customers fully understand your offerings, value proposition, what you stand for, and how to take action. Identify your B2B marketing tactics. Once you’ve selected your marketing channels, your next step is to identify the specific tactics you’ll use to reach your target B2B customers. Four examples of tactics to implement include the following: Offer a freemium service or a trial period so B2B customers can experience the impact of your offerings on their operations. Take an account-based marketing approach by networking with contacts at key business targets, building rapport with them, personalizing the communications, and encouraging sales. Use cause-based marketing to design products and campaigns in collaboration with charitable organizations, demonstrating your business's commitment to creating a better world. Create a more impactful, detailed customer journey for a longer sales cycle. You can do this by delivering content that supports buying decisions and emphasizes the outcomes and benefits your products offer. Business Marketing B2B Marketing: Definition + Strategies B2B Marketing: Definition + Strategies Written by Coursera Staff • Updated on Nov 6, 2026 Discover B2B marketing, common B2B marketing channels, and how to build your strategy. Key takeaways Business-to-business (B2B) marketing is a type of marketing that businesses use when focusing on promoting goods and services to other businesses rather than to consumers, and it involves strategies such as B2B content marketing, social media marketing, and email marketing. B2B content marketing helps you rank in search engine results, which can increase your visibility with potential customers, and help build trust using various types of content, including explainer videos, educational content regarding industry trends, and customer testimonials. You can build your B2B digital marketing strategy by identifying your brand positioning and how set your brand apart from its competition, describing your target buyers, building your brand voice, and selecting B2B marketing channels. B2B marketing means targeting decision-makers at organizations, typically based on logical motics such as return on investment. Read on to learn more about B2B marketing, including common strategies and how to develop a marketing plan for your business. Afterward, if you want to build foundational marketing skills, consider enrolling in the Google Digital Marketing & E-commerce Professional Certificate . It takes an average of six months to complete at a flexible pace and offers opportunities to learn digital marketing fundamentals, become familiar with spreadsheets, and develop skills in social media marketing, relationship management, and media planning. What is B2B marketing? Business-to-business, or B2B, marketing is the process of promoting products and services to other companies to help them improve their operations. It helps create demand and brand awareness. B2B companies often offer products and services such as software-as-a-service (SaaS), professional services, consulting, manufacturing, and wholesale products.Some B2B companies are large and also offer products directly to consumers. For example, Amazon, Meta, and Apple all blur the lines between the two and require both B2B and business-to-consumer (B2C) marketing. Other real-world examples of B2B companies include: Microsoft Salesforce Mailchimp When selling to other companies, remember that B2B marketing involves considerations and best practices that differ from those associated with marketing to individual consumers (B2C). For example, B2B customers generally look for products and services that will contribute to a healthier bottom line while avoiding investments with a low likelihood of a return. Considering that businesses may be responsible for payroll and other large business expenses, there may be more at stake for B2B than B2C customers, so when marketing, you’d want to bear this difference in mind. Explore other differences in the chart below: B2B B2C What it is Marketing to the decision makers at organizations Marketing to individual consumers Product examples Software, office equipment, and supplies, co-working spaces Food, clothing, electronic devices, books, media subscriptions Service examples Consulting and training, web or graphic design, product distribution, ad campaign management Tutoring, hair styling, health care, home cleaning, car repair Buying motives Logic: What’s the financial ROI of an investment? What’s the expertise level of a service provider? Emotions: Will this product solve a problem or fulfill a desire? Sales cycle Longer sales cycle as decision makers consider the return on investment Shorter sales cycle, especially for impulse purchases Market research focus Firmographics of businesses and psychographics of decision makers Demographics and psychographics of individual consumers 7 common B2B digital marketing strategies B2B marketing strategies, which include B2B-focused content marketing, social media marketing, email marketing, and event marketing, can help connect buyers with products and services using a combination of data and content to achieve results. Discover some common B2B marketing channels , both digital and offline, as well as best practices for promoting your business on these channels to help plan your next steps. B2B content marketing Content marketing , particularly SEO content on your website , is an effective way to reach a target audience of B2B customers. Focused content can build trust with decision-makers, increase your website’s ranking in search engine results, and provide a basis for marketing efforts on other channels. Different types of content that work well for a B2B audience include the following: Thought leadership and educational content on important industry trends and strategies that your target B2B customers can use Videos explaining how your products and services can help B2B customers Webpages explaining your company’s method of prioritizing diversity, equity, and inclusion, and what these efforts mean for your target B2B customer Customer testimonials Read more: How to Develop a Content Strategy: A Step-by-Step Guide B2B social media marketing To attract B2B customers on different social media platforms, adopt practices that are specific to a business-oriented audience, and leverage the power of videos for product demonstrations, tutorials, industry highlights, behind-the-scenes content, case studies, “about us” stories, and business-building strategies. Additional strategies to consider include the following: Tailor your posts to each platform. For example, you could repurpose long-form content into a Tweetable tip, an infographic for Instagram, and an excerpt for LinkedIn. Set up in-platform purchase and subscription options on social media. Algorithms may promote this content to more viewers, as it doesn’t lead users away from the platform. Partner with micro-influencers in your niche (users with 10,000 to 99,999 followers) to gain access to their loyal, targeted followers. B2B podcasting Podcasting can be a great way to reach B2B customers and provide them with informative content in audio format. By discussing topics that help businesses thrive, your podcast can establish you as a B2B thought leader. Topics might include: Leadership strategies Industry news and trends B2B customer success stories E-commerce best practices B2B email marketing Email marketing can be an effective way to build relationships with B2B customers and convert leads (potential customers or prospects) into buyers. Artificial intelligence (AI) tools can help optimize email campaigns, drive increased personalization, and automate content generation directed to specific buyers. Additional email marketing strategies to consider include the following: To build your subscriber base, design a lead-capture landing page that addresses a top-of-mind problem or need for your target B2B customers and promises a solution in the form of a lead magnet, such as a downloadable report or a free video tutorial. Make sure your lead magnet actually provides the solution promised on the landing page and demonstrates how your company can help other businesses operate more smoothly. Divide your subscribers into smaller segments based on their roles within a decision-making unit, the kind of business, where they are in the customer journey, and other factors, so that you can tailor email marketing content accordingly. Include attention-grabbing words in your email subject lines, such as solutions to a problem or product offers, to encourage B2B email subscribers to click. Craft each email message to deliver value and lead subscribers to a purchase decision. Emails can expound upon social media and content marketing pieces, offer exclusive information, invite subscribers to complete a survey, shape future content, and announce new products. B2B event marketing Hosting, attending, and sponsoring events, either in person or online, can increase your brand’s exposure and generate qualified leads. Successful B2B events can take on many forms, including: Workshops, classes, and webinars on topics of interest to your target B2B customers Networking events, exhibitions, and trade shows, where you can build relationships with company decision-makers in your target market and introduce them to your products and services Professional conferences where your target B2B customers can learn new information and network with peers Parties, performances, dinners, and other social events to entertain target B2B customers and offer individualized or VIP experiences B2B marketing word-of-mouth and referrals Loyal and satisfied customers can be a great source of new leads, especially in B2B marketing. When a business recommends your product or service and can quantify a positive outcome, it carries authority. To encourage customers to make thoughtful referrals, you might offer referral bonuses or set up an affiliate program . Paid search Paid search, also known as pay-per-click (PPC) advertising, refers to a strategy that marketers use to leverage search engine results pages (SERPs). Ads typically appear at the top or bottom of a search engine results page (SERP), and when an internet user clicks on an ad, the advertiser pays a fee. This strategy can support your B2B efforts by targeting ads to businesses looking for a specific solution that you can provide. To succeed, you'll need compelling ad copy, strategic keywords (search queries B2B customers use to search the internet), and data-driven insights. Build your B2B digital marketing agency strategy A B2B marketing strategy can have a measurable impact on your business as you expand into new markets for your products and services. Follow the steps below to begin building your B2B marketing strategy, starting with positioning your brand to stand out amongst your competitors. Determine your brand’s positioning. Brand positioning is the combination of factors that differentiate your brand from competitors in the minds of your ideal customers. Clear brand positioning can help you build brand equity and, thus, make your B2B marketing efforts more effective. How will your B2B products and services help businesses succeed better than competitors’ offerings ? What associations, ideas, feelings, and concepts will your brand create in customers’ minds? What will they believe about your products and services? What factors will inspire loyalty in your customers? How to create a B2B marketing agency brand positioning statement Use answers to the above questions to craft a brand positioning statement: [B2B audience] will choose [product/service] to experience [benefits and outcomes], because [B2B audience’s beliefs]. Describe your buyer personas. Create a distinct and detailed buyer persona for each type of business you serve. Start by gathering firmographic data (how different organizations behave) on the kinds of businesses you want to target, as well as psychographic data (how individuals behave) on decision-making units within these businesses, using the prompts below to start. Firmographic data on businesses: How would you describe the industry your target business is a part of, including key players, trends, opportunities, and untapped markets? What kinds of products or services do your target businesses offer? What types of consumers do they serve? How many employees work at these businesses? What’s the average annual revenue? How are these organizations structured in terms of leadership, departments, teams, and individual contributors? Psychographic data on decision-makers: What is the role of each decision-maker within your target businesses, and how will they interact with you during the sales process? What motivates these decision-makers professionally? What inspires them to work in this industry? Develop a brand voice. Your brand’s voice is essential to connecting with customers, personalizing their experience with your B2B products and services, and inspiring their trust in your business solutions. The brand voice will shape how you craft every email, social media caption, video script, piece of long-form content, web copy, and more. When conducting B2B market research, collect insights into the language that company decision-makers use to describe their challenges and goals. Draw from customer language to develop a distinct, empathetic brand voice. Select your B2B marketing channels. While it’s a good practice to build a presence and create customer experiences on multiple channels, don’t feel pressured to be on every channel . Prioritize the channels where your target B2B customers are most likely to engage with your content. Create a seamless omnichannel customer journey to increase loyalty and retention rates. Make sure you tell your full brand story on every channel so that your target B2B customers fully understand your offerings, value proposition, what you stand for, and how to take action. Identify your B2B marketing tactics. Once you’ve selected your marketing channels, your next step is to identify the specific tactics you’ll use to reach your target B2B customers. Four examples of tactics to implement include the following: Offer a freemium service or a trial period so B2B customers can experience the impact of your offerings on their operations. Take an account-based marketing approach by networking with contacts at key business targets, building rapport with them, personalizing the communications, and encouraging sales. Use cause-based marketing to design products and campaigns in collaboration with charitable organizations, demonstrating your business's commitment to creating a better world. Create a more impactful, detailed customer journey for a longer sales cycle. You can do this by delivering content that supports buying decisions and emphasizes the outcomes and benefits your products offer. What kinds of products or services do your target businesses offer? What types of consumers do they serve? How many employees work at these businesses? What’s the average annual revenue? How are these organizations structured in terms of leadership, departments, teams, and individual contributors? Psychographic data on decision-makers: What is the role of each decision-maker within your target businesses, and how will they interact with you during the sales process? What motivates these decision-makers professionally? What inspires them to work in this industry? Develop a brand voice. Your brand’s voice is essential to connecting with customers, personalizing their experience with your B2B products and services, and inspiring their trust in your business solutions. The brand voice will shape how you craft every email, social media caption, video script, piece of long-form content, web copy, and more. When conducting B2B market research, collect insights into the language that company decision-makers use to describe their challenges and goals. Draw from customer language to develop a distinct, empathetic brand voice. Select your B2B marketing channels. While it’s a good practice to build a presence and create customer experiences on multiple channels, don’t feel pressured to be on every channel . Prioritize the channels where your target B2B customers are most likely to engage with your content. Create a seamless omnichannel customer journey to increase loyalty and retention rates. Make sure you tell your full brand story on every channel so that your target B2B customers fully understand your offerings, value proposition, what you stand for, and how to take action. Identify your B2B marketing tactics. Once you’ve selected your marketing channels, your next step is to identify the specific tactics you’ll use to reach your target B2B customers. Four examples of tactics to implement include the following: Offer a freemium service or a trial period so B2B customers can experience the impact of your offerings on their operations. Take an account-based marketing approach by networking with contacts at key business targets, building rapport with them, personalizing the communications, and encouraging sales. Use cause-based marketing to design products and campaigns in collaboration with charitable organizations, demonstrating your business's commitment to creating a better world. Create a more impactful, detailed customer journey for a longer sales cycle. You can do this by delivering content that supports buying decisions and emphasizes the outcomes and benefits your products offer. # My Health Record B2B Gateway

My Health Record is a secure online summary of an individual’s health information and is available to all Australians.

Through the Business to Business (B2B) Gateway, healthcare providers can access timely information and clinical documents about their patients, such as shared health summaries, discharge summaries, prescription and dispense records, pathology reports, diagnostic imaging reports and other clinical documents.

### My Health Record Connecting Systems Security Conformance Profile Implementation Timeline[#](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/services/my-health-record/my-health-record-b2b-gateway#my-health-record-connecting-systems-security-conformance-profile "my-health-record-connecting-systems-security-conformance-profile")

For information and updates refer to: [My Health Record Connecting Systems Security Conformance Profile Implementation Timeline](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/newsroom/announcements/my-health-record-connecting-systems-security-conformance-profile-implementation-timeline "My Health Record Connecting Systems Security Conformance Profile Implementation Timeline").

## Get Started[#](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/services/my-health-record/my-health-record-b2b-gateway#get-started "get-started")

If you want to connect to the Healthcare Identifiers (HI) Service or integrate with My Health Record, follow the steps on the Get Started page.

[Get Started](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/get-started "Get started")

## Registration Overview[#](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/services/my-health-record/my-health-record-b2b-gateway#registration-overview "registration-overview")

Integration with My Health Record is carried out through a two-step process:

1.   Integrate with the HI Service,
2.   Integrate with the My Health Record system.

## Pre-requisites[#](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/services/my-health-record/my-health-record-b2b-gateway#pre-requisites "pre-requisites")

To begin, you must have completed the following:

1.   [HI Service Developer Registration](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/services/healthcare-identifiers-service-hi "Healthcare Identifiers Service (HI Service)")
2.   [My Health Record Developer Registration](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/my-health-record-b2b-gateway-registration "My Health Record B2B Gateway - Registration")

**Important**  
Please initiate the registration processes for both HI and the My Health Record system immediately, as there will be some turnaround time for responses, and you will require Test C.

## Prepare for development[#](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/services/my-health-record/my-health-record-b2b-gateway#prepare-for-development "prepare-for-development")

If you are interested in integrating your software with the My Health Record system, we recommend starting by reviewing our [Getting started education modules](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/getting-started-education-modules "Getting started education modules").

**Pre-Reading**

*   [Welcome Pack materials](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/my-health-record-software-vendor-welcome-pack-v1-0 "My Health Record Software Vendor Welcome Pack v1.0")
*   [Software Vendor Guide to the Connection Process](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/my-health-record-software-vendor-guide-to-the-connection-process-v2-3 "My Health Record - Software Vendor Guide to the Connection Process v2.3")
*   [Software Vendor Support Contacts](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/node/9089)

**Read through My Health Record B2B Developer Guides**

*   [Find whether a My Health Record exists](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/my-health-record-b2b-gateway-find-whether-a-my-health-record-exists "My Health Record B2B Gateway - Find whether a My Health Record exists")
*   [Gain access to a My Health Record](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/my-health-record-b2b-gateway-gain-access-to-a-my-health-record "My Health Record B2B Gateway - Gain access to a My Health Record")
*   [Get Documents and View Document](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/my-health-record-b2b-gateway-get-patient-document-list-and-view-document "My Health Record B2B Gateway - Get Patient Document List and View Document")
*   [Get Views](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/my-health-record-b2b-gateway-get-views "My Health Record B2B Gateway - Get Views")

*   [Supersede Document](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/my-health-record-b2b-gateway-supersede-document "My Health Record B2B Gateway - Supersede document")
*   [Remove Document](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/my-health-record-b2b-gateway-remove-document "My Health Record B2B Gateway - Remove document")

To continue reading, go to My Health Record B2B Gateway – Registration Developer Guide below.

#### [Pharmacist Shared Medicines List (PSML)[#](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/services/my-health-record/my-health-record-b2b-gateway#pharmacist-shared-medicines-list-psml "pharmacist-shared-medicines-list-psml")](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/pharmacist-shared-medicines-list-psml)

The Pharmacist Shared Medicines List (PSML) is a clinical document type supported by the My Health Record system.

#### [What are the test endpoints?[#](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/services/my-health-record/my-health-record-b2b-gateway#what-are-the-test-endpoints "what-are-the-test-endpoints")](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/what-are-the-test-endpoints)

HI Service and My Health Record test endpoint access information:

#### [HI Service - IHI Lookup[#](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/services/my-health-record/my-health-record-b2b-gateway#hi-service-ihi-lookup "hi-service-ihi-lookup")](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/hi-service-ihi-lookup)

Your software will need to conduct lookups for Individual Healthcare Identifiers (IHIs) for patients.

#### [HI Service - IHI Lookup - Test Cases[#](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/services/my-health-record/my-health-record-b2b-gateway#hi-service-ihi-lookup-test-cases "hi-service-ihi-lookup-test-cases")](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/hi-service-ihi-lookup-test-cases)

#### [My Health Record Connecting Systems - Security Conformance Profile - FAQs[#](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/services/my-health-record/my-health-record-b2b-gateway#my-health-record-connecting-systems-security-conformance-profile-2 "my-health-record-connecting-systems-security-conformance-profile-2")](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/my-health-record-connecting-systems-security-conformance-profile-faqs)

The Security Requirements for My Health Record Connecting Systems Conformance Profile contains software requirements that harden clinical information systems from cyber security attacks, uplift information security and protect patient information and your software product.

#### [1007 - Personally Controlled Electronic Health Record (PCEHR) identifiers - OID Register[#](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/services/my-health-record/my-health-record-b2b-gateway#1007-personally-controlled-electronic-health-record-pcehr-identi "1007-personally-controlled-electronic-health-record-pcehr-identi")](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/1007-personally-controlled-electronic-health-record-pcehr-identifiers-oid-register)

# My Health Record B2B Gateway

My Health Record is a secure online summary of an individual’s health information and is available to all Australians.

Through the Business to Business (B2B) Gateway, healthcare providers can access timely information and clinical documents about their patients, such as shared health summaries, discharge summaries, prescription and dispense records, pathology reports, diagnostic imaging reports and other clinical documents.

### My Health Record Connecting Systems Security Conformance Profile Implementation Timeline[#](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/services/my-health-record/my-health-record-b2b-gateway#my-health-record-connecting-systems-security-conformance-profile "my-health-record-connecting-systems-security-conformance-profile")

For information and updates refer to: [My Health Record Connecting Systems Security Conformance Profile Implementation Timeline](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/newsroom/announcements/my-health-record-connecting-systems-security-conformance-profile-implementation-timeline "My Health Record Connecting Systems Security Conformance Profile Implementation Timeline").

## Registration Overview[#](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/services/my-health-record/my-health-record-b2b-gateway#registration-overview "registration-overview")

Integration with My Health Record is carried out through a two-step process:

1.   Integrate with the HI Service,
2.   Integrate with the My Health Record system.

## Pre-requisites[#](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/services/my-health-record/my-health-record-b2b-gateway#pre-requisites "pre-requisites")

To begin, you must have completed the following:

2.   [My Health Record Developer Registration](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/resources/my-health-record-b2b-gateway-registration "My Health Record B2B Gateway - Registration")

**Important**  
Please initiate the registration processes for both HI and the My Health Record system immediately, as there will be some turnaround time for responses, and you will require Test C.

Business Marketing B2B Marketing: Definition + Strategies B2B Marketing: Definition + Strategies Written by Coursera Staff • Updated on Nov 6, 2026 Discover B2B marketing, common B2B marketing channels, and how to build your strategy. Key takeaways Business-to-business (B2B) marketing is a type of marketing that businesses use when focusing on promoting goods and services to other businesses rather than to consumers, and it involves strategies such as B2B content marketing, social media marketing, and email marketing. B2B content marketing helps you rank in search engine results, which can increase your visibility with potential customers, and help build trust using various types of content, including explainer videos, educational content regarding industry trends, and customer testimonials. You can build your B2B digital marketing strategy by identifying your brand positioning and how set your brand apart from its competition, describing your target buyers, building your brand voice, and selecting B2B marketing channels. B2B marketing means targeting decision-makers at organizations, typically based on logical motics such as return on investment. Read on to learn more about B2B marketing, including common strategies and how to develop a marketing plan for your business. Afterward, if you want to build foundational marketing skills, consider enrolling in the Google Digital Marketing & E-commerce Professional Certificate . It takes an average of six months to complete at a flexible pace and offers opportunities to learn digital marketing fundamentals, become familiar with spreadsheets, and develop skills in social media marketing, relationship management, and media planning. What is B2B marketing? Business-to-business, or B2B, marketing is the process of promoting products and services to other companies to help them improve their operations. It helps create demand and brand awareness. B2B companies often offer products and services such as software-as-a-service (SaaS), professional services, consulting, manufacturing, and wholesale products.Some B2B companies are large and also offer products directly to consumers. For example, Amazon, Meta, and Apple all blur the lines between the two and require both B2B and business-to-consumer (B2C) marketing. Other real-world examples of B2B companies include: Microsoft Salesforce Mailchimp When selling to other companies, remember that B2B marketing involves considerations and best practices that differ from those associated with marketing to individual consumers (B2C). For example, B2B customers generally look for products and services that will contribute to a healthier bottom line while avoiding investments with a low likelihood of a return. Considering that businesses may be responsible for payroll and other large business expenses, there may be more at stake for B2B than B2C customers, so when marketing, you’d want to bear this difference in mind. Explore other differences in the chart below: B2B B2C What it is Marketing to the decision makers at organizations Marketing to individual consumers Product examples Software, office equipment, and supplies, co-working spaces Food, clothing, electronic devices, books, media subscriptions Service examples Consulting and training, web or graphic design, product distribution, ad campaign management Tutoring, hair styling, health care, home cleaning, car repair Buying motives Logic: What’s the financial ROI of an investment? What’s the expertise level of a service provider? Emotions: Will this product solve a problem or fulfill a desire? Sales cycle Longer sales cycle as decision makers consider the return on investment Shorter sales cycle, especially for impulse purchases Market research focus Firmographics of businesses and psychographics of decision makers Demographics and psychographics of individual consumers 7 common B2B digital marketing strategies B2B marketing strategies, which include B2B-focused content marketing, social media marketing, email marketing, and event marketing, can help connect buyers with products and services using a combination of data and content to achieve results. Discover some common B2B marketing channels , both digital and offline, as well as best practices for promoting your business on these channels to help plan your next steps. B2B content marketing Content marketing , particularly SEO content on your website , is an effective way to reach a target audience of B2B customers. Focused content can build trust with decision-makers, increase your website’s ranking in search engine results, and provide a basis for marketing efforts on other channels. Different types of content that work well for a B2B audience include the following: Thought leadership and educational content on important industry trends and strategies that your target B2B customers can use Videos explaining how your products and services can help B2B customers Webpages explaining your company’s method of prioritizing diversity, equity, and inclusion, and what these efforts mean for your target B2B customer Customer testimonials Read more: How to Develop a Content Strategy: A Step-by-Step Guide B2B social media marketing To attract B2B customers on different social media platforms, adopt practices that are specific to a business-oriented audience, and leverage the power of videos for product demonstrations, tutorials, industry highlights, behind-the-scenes content, case studies, “about us” stories, and business-building strategies. Additional strategies to consider include the following: Tailor your posts to each platform. For example, you could repurpose long-form content into a Tweetable tip, an infographic for Instagram, and an excerpt for LinkedIn. Set up in-platform purchase and subscription options on social media. Algorithms may promote this content to more viewers, as it doesn’t lead users away from the platform. Partner with micro-influencers in your niche (users with 10,000 to 99,999 followers) to gain access to their loyal, targeted followers. B2B podcasting Podcasting can be a great way to reach B2B customers and provide them with informative content in audio format. By discussing topics that help businesses thrive, your podcast can establish you as a B2B thought leader. Topics might include: Leadership strategies Industry news and trends B2B customer success stories E-commerce best practices B2B email marketing Email marketing can be an effective way to build relationships with B2B customers and convert leads (potential customers or prospects) into buyers. Artificial intelligence (AI) tools can help optimize email campaigns, drive increased personalization, and automate content generation directed to specific buyers. Additional email marketing strategies to consider include the following: To build your subscriber base, design a lead-capture landing page that addresses a top-of-mind problem or need for your target B2B customers and promises a solution in the form of a lead magnet, such as a downloadable report or a free video tutorial. Make sure your lead magnet actually provides the solution promised on the landing page and demonstrates how your company can help other businesses operate more smoothly. Divide your subscribers into smaller segments based on their roles within a decision-making unit, the kind of business, where they are in the customer journey, and other factors, so that you can tailor email marketing content accordingly. Include attention-grabbing words in your email subject lines, such as solutions to a problem or product offers, to encourage B2B email subscribers to click. Craft each email message to deliver value and lead subscribers to a purchase decision. Emails can expound upon social media and content marketing pieces, offer exclusive information, invite subscribers to complete a survey, shape future content, and announce new products. B2B event marketing Hosting, attending, and sponsoring events, either in person or online, can increase your brand’s exposure and generate qualified leads. Successful B2B events can take on many forms, including: Workshops, classes, and webinars on topics of interest to your target B2B customers Networking events, exhibitions, and trade shows, where you can build relationships with company decision-makers in your target market and introduce them to your products and services Professional conferences where your target B2B customers can learn new information and network with peers Parties, performances, dinners, and other social events to entertain target B2B customers and offer individualized or VIP experiences B2B marketing word-of-mouth and referrals Loyal and satisfied customers can be a great source of new leads, especially in B2B marketing. When a business recommends your product or service and can quantify a positive outcome, it carries authority. To encourage customers to make thoughtful referrals, you might offer referral bonuses or set up an affiliate program . Paid search Paid search, also known as pay-per-click (PPC) advertising, refers to a strategy that marketers use to leverage search engine results pages (SERPs). Ads typically appear at the top or bottom of a search engine results page (SERP), and when an internet user clicks on an ad, the advertiser pays a fee. This strategy can support your B2B efforts by targeting ads to businesses looking for a specific solution that you can provide. To succeed, you'll need compelling ad copy, strategic keywords (search queries B2B customers use to search the internet), and data-driven insights. Build your B2B digital marketing agency strategy A B2B marketing strategy can have a measurable impact on your business as you expand into new markets for your products and services. Follow the steps below to begin building your B2B marketing strategy, starting with positioning your brand to stand out amongst your competitors. Determine your brand’s positioning. Brand positioning is the combination of factors that differentiate your brand from competitors in the minds of your ideal customers. Clear brand positioning can help you build brand equity and, thus, make your B2B marketing efforts more effective. How will your B2B products and services help businesses succeed better than competitors’ offerings ? What associations, ideas, feelings, and concepts will your brand create in customers’ minds? What will they believe about your products and services? What factors will inspire loyalty in your customers? How to create a B2B marketing agency brand positioning statement Use answers to the above questions to craft a brand positioning statement: [B2B audience] will choose [product/service] to experience [benefits and outcomes], because [B2B audience’s beliefs]. Describe your buyer personas. Create a distinct and detailed buyer persona for each type of business you serve. Start by gathering firmographic data (how different organizations behave) on the kinds of businesses you want to target, as well as psychographic data (how individuals behave) on decision-making units within these businesses, using the prompts below to start. Firmographic data on businesses: How would you describe the industry your target business is a part of, including key players, trends, opportunities, and untapped markets? What kinds of products or services do your target businesses offer? What types of consumers do they serve? How many employees work at these businesses? What’s the average annual revenue? How are these organizations structured in terms of leadership, departments, teams, and individual contributors? Psychographic data on decision-makers: What is the role of each decision-maker within your target businesses, and how will they interact with you during the sales process? What motivates these decision-makers professionally? What inspires them to work in this industry? Develop a brand voice. Your brand’s voice is essential to connecting with customers, personalizing their experience with your B2B products and services, and inspiring their trust in your business solutions. The brand voice will shape how you craft every email, social media caption, video script, piece of long-form content, web copy, and more. When conducting B2B market research, collect insights into the language that company decision-makers use to describe their challenges and goals. Draw from customer language to develop a distinct, empathetic brand voice. Select your B2B marketing channels. While it’s a good practice to build a presence and create customer experiences on multiple channels, don’t feel pressured to be on every channel . Prioritize the channels where your target B2B customers are most likely to engage with your content. Create a seamless omnichannel customer journey to increase loyalty and retention rates. Make sure you tell your full brand story on every channel so that your target B2B customers fully understand your offerings, value proposition, what you stand for, and how to take action. Identify your B2B marketing tactics. Once you’ve selected your marketing channels, your next step is to identify the specific tactics you’ll use to reach your target B2B customers. Four examples of tactics to implement include the following: Offer a freemium service or a trial period so B2B customers can experience the impact of your offerings on their operations. Take an account-based marketing approach by networking with contacts at key business targets, building rapport with them, personalizing the communications, and encouraging sales. Use cause-based marketing to design products and campaigns in collaboration with charitable organizations, demonstrating your business's commitment to creating a better world. Create a more impactful, detailed customer journey for a longer sales cycle. You can do this by delivering content that supports buying decisions and emphasizes the outcomes and benefits your products offer. You can build your B2B digital marketing strategy by identifying your brand positioning and how set your brand apart from its competition, describing your target buyers, building your brand voice, and selecting B2B marketing channels. B2B marketing means targeting decision-makers at organizations, typically based on logical motics such as return on investment. Read on to learn more about B2B marketing, including common strategies and how to develop a marketing plan for your business. What is B2B marketing? Business-to-business, or B2B, marketing is the process of promoting products and services to other companies to help them improve their operations. It helps create demand and brand awareness. B2B companies often offer products and services such as software-as-a-service (SaaS), professional services, consulting, manufacturing, and wholesale products.Some B2B companies are large and also offer products directly to consumers. For example, Amazon, Meta, and Apple all blur the lines between the two and require both B2B and business-to-consumer (B2C) marketing. Other real-world examples of B2B companies include: Microsoft Salesforce Mailchimp When selling to other companies, remember that B2B marketing involves considerations and best practices that differ from those associated with marketing to individual consumers (B2C). For example, B2B customers generally look for products and services that will contribute to a healthier bottom line while avoiding investments with a low likelihood of a return. Considering that businesses may be responsible for payroll and other large business expenses, there may be more at stake for B2B than B2C customers, so when marketing, you’d want to bear this difference in mind. What’s the expertise level of a service provider? Emotions: Will this product solve a problem or fulfill a desire? Sales cycle Longer sales cycle as decision makers consider the return on investment Shorter sales cycle, especially for impulse purchases Market research focus Firmographics of businesses and psychographics of decision makers Demographics and psychographics of individual consumers 7 common B2B digital marketing strategies B2B marketing strategies, which include B2B-focused content marketing, social media marketing, email marketing, and event marketing, can help connect buyers with products and services using a combination of data and content to achieve results. Different types of content that work well for a B2B audience include the following: Thought leadership and educational content on important industry trends and strategies that your target B2B customers can use Videos explaining how your products and services can help B2B customers Webpages explaining your company’s method of prioritizing diversity, equity, and inclusion, and what these efforts mean for your target B2B customer Customer testimonials Read more: How to Develop a Content Strategy: A Step-by-Step Guide B2B social media marketing To attract B2B customers on different social media platforms, adopt practices that are specific to a business-oriented audience, and leverage the power of videos for product demonstrations, tutorials, industry highlights, behind-the-scenes content, case studies, “about us” stories, and business-building strategies. Additional strategies to consider include the following: Tailor your posts to each platform. For example, you could repurpose long-form content into a Tweetable tip, an infographic for Instagram, and an excerpt for LinkedIn. Set up in-platform purchase and subscription options on social media. Algorithms may promote this content to more viewers, as it doesn’t lead users away from the platform. Partner with micro-influencers in your niche (users with 10,000 to 99,999 followers) to gain access to their loyal, targeted followers. B2B podcasting Podcasting can be a great way to reach B2B customers and provide them with informative content in audio format. By discussing topics that help businesses thrive, your podcast can establish you as a B2B thought leader. Topics might include: Leadership strategies Industry news and trends B2B customer success stories E-commerce best practices B2B email marketing Email marketing can be an effective way to build relationships with B2B customers and convert leads (potential customers or prospects) into buyers. Artificial intelligence (AI) tools can help optimize email campaigns, drive increased personalization, and automate content generation directed to specific buyers. Additional email marketing strategies to consider include the following: To build your subscriber base, design a lead-capture landing page that addresses a top-of-mind problem or need for your target B2B customers and promises a solution in the form of a lead magnet, such as a downloadable report or a free video tutorial. Make sure your lead magnet actually provides the solution promised on the landing page and demonstrates how your company can help other businesses operate more smoothly. Divide your subscribers into smaller segments based on their roles within a decision-making unit, the kind of business, where they are in the customer journey, and other factors, so that you can tailor email marketing content accordingly. Include attention-grabbing words in your email subject lines, such as solutions to a problem or product offers, to encourage B2B email subscribers to click. Craft each email message to deliver value and lead subscribers to a purchase decision. Emails can expound upon social media and content marketing pieces, offer exclusive information, invite subscribers to complete a survey, shape future content, and announce new products. B2B event marketing Hosting, attending, and sponsoring events, either in person or online, can increase your brand’s exposure and generate qualified leads. Successful B2B events can take on many forms, including: Workshops, classes, and webinars on topics of interest to your target B2B customers Networking events, exhibitions, and trade shows, where you can build relationships with company decision-makers in your target market and introduce them to your products and services Professional conferences where your target B2B customers can learn new information and network with peers Parties, performances, dinners, and other social events to entertain target B2B customers and offer individualized or VIP experiences B2B marketing word-of-mouth and referrals Loyal and satisfied customers can be a great source of new leads, especially in B2B marketing. When a business recommends your product or service and can quantify a positive outcome, it carries authority. To encourage customers to make thoughtful referrals, you might offer referral bonuses or set up an affiliate program . Paid search Paid search, also known as pay-per-click (PPC) advertising, refers to a strategy that marketers use to leverage search engine results pages (SERPs). Ads typically appear at the top or bottom of a search engine results page (SERP), and when an internet user clicks on an ad, the advertiser pays a fee. This strategy can support your B2B efforts by targeting ads to businesses looking for a specific solution that you can provide. To succeed, you'll need compelling ad copy, strategic keywords (search queries B2B customers use to search the internet), and data-driven insights. Follow the steps below to begin building your B2B marketing strategy, starting with positioning your brand to stand out amongst your competitors. Determine your brand’s positioning. Brand positioning is the combination of factors that differentiate your brand from competitors in the minds of your ideal customers. Clear brand positioning can help you build brand equity and, thus, make your B2B marketing efforts more effective. How will your B2B products and services help businesses succeed better than competitors’ offerings ? What associations, ideas, feelings, and concepts will your brand create in customers’ minds? What will they believe about your products and services? What factors will inspire loyalty in your customers? How to create a B2B marketing agency brand positioning statement Use answers to the above questions to craft a brand positioning statement: [B2B audience] will choose [product/service] to experience [benefits and outcomes], because [B2B audience’s beliefs]. Describe your buyer personas. Create a distinct and detailed buyer persona for each type of business you serve. Start by gathering firmographic data (how different organizations behave) on the kinds of businesses you want to target, as well as psychographic data (how individuals behave) on decision-making units within these businesses, using the prompts below to start. Firmographic data on businesses: How would you describe the industry your target business is a part of, including key players, trends, opportunities, and untapped markets? What kinds of products or services do your target businesses offer? What types of consumers do they serve? How many employees work at these businesses? What’s the average annual revenue? How are these organizations structured in terms of leadership, departments, teams, and individual contributors? Psychographic data on decision-makers: What is the role of each decision-maker within your target businesses, and how will they interact with you during the sales process? What motivates these decision-makers professionally? What inspires them to work in this industry? Develop a brand voice. Your brand’s voice is essential to connecting with customers, personalizing their experience with your B2B products and services, and inspiring their trust in your business solutions. The brand voice will shape how you craft every email, social media caption, video script, piece of long-form content, web copy, and more. When conducting B2B market research, collect insights into the language that company decision-makers use to describe their challenges and goals. Draw from customer language to develop a distinct, empathetic brand voice. Select your B2B marketing channels. While it’s a good practice to build a presence and create customer experiences on multiple channels, don’t feel pressured to be on every channel . Prioritize the channels where your target B2B customers are most likely to engage with your content. Create a seamless omnichannel customer journey to increase loyalty and retention rates. Make sure you tell your full brand story on every channel so that your target B2B customers fully understand your offerings, value proposition, what you stand for, and how to take action. Identify your B2B marketing tactics. Once you’ve selected your marketing channels, your next step is to identify the specific tactics you’ll use to reach your target B2B customers. Four examples of tactics to implement include the following: Offer a freemium service or a trial period so B2B customers can experience the impact of your offerings on their operations. Take an account-based marketing approach by networking with contacts at key business targets, building rapport with them, personalizing the communications, and encouraging sales. Use cause-based marketing to design products and campaigns in collaboration with charitable organizations, demonstrating your business's commitment to creating a better world. Create a more impactful, detailed customer journey for a longer sales cycle. You can do this by delivering content that supports buying decisions and emphasizes the outcomes and benefits your products offer.
